name: Array of Corporeal Brilliance
reason: A body-tempering array from the Blackrock Peak storyline was given the coined Western-fantasy name 'Array of Corporeal Brilliance'; the exact source term was not identified in the evidence.
description: A magic array designed by Master Robert, a respected master of array design, for Blackrock Peak's outer disciples (Ep 246). It powers a secret attunement sanctum where outer disciples temper their bodies; only a few peaks such as Blackrock, Skytop and Azure had such sanctums.

name: Twins Chaos Cyclone
reason: No source counterpart was identified in the evidence; the name appears to be an adaptation coinage for Cecil's signature all-angle attack technique.
description: Cecil's devastating signature technique, unleashed during his duel in Eps 250-251. It attacks from every angle over a massive area, and on a battlefield it could reportedly wipe out entire armies caught in its range.

name: Grade Two Adept
reason: The source cultivation sub-level 'Xiantian Realm Stage Two' was localized as 'Grade Two Adept', in keeping with the show's rendering of the Xiantian Realm as the Adept Realm.
description: A sub-level of the Adept Realm. Per the master sheet it was Zane's level when he achieved 100 waves on the Seven-Star Platform.

name: Adept’s Pinnacle
reason: The source's 'Xiantian Full Circle' (the perfected peak of the Xiantian Realm) was localized as 'Adept's Pinnacle', matching the show's Adept Realm tier naming.
description: The peak sub-level of the Adept Realm, bordering the Soul Realm. In Ep 253 Finn is at the Adept's Pinnacle, his power already knocking on the door of the Soul Realm, just like Nicholas.

name: Uncle Kent
reason: The source's 'Uncle Lin', the old guardian associated with the technique library, was localized with the US-style name 'Kent' while keeping the familiar 'Uncle' honorific.
description: An elder tied to a forbidden fist manual: of the three who obtained it, two failed to master it and the third was forbidden from even practicing it by Uncle Kent himself (Ep 256). He corresponds to the source's Uncle Lin, the old man of the Heavenly Book Pavilion who blocked one practitioner of the Sky Demon God Fist.

name: Hymns of Warding
reason: Zhou Dan's protective golden 'Righteous Song' script was localized as 'Hymns of Warding', keeping the musical, protective sense; Ep 259's title 'The Hymn of Justice' confirms the mapping.
description: Protective written hymns that Richard inscribes with his Runic Brush during his duel in Ep 259; each hymn absorbs several hits before cracking and shattering, and they work alongside his offensive Deathly Canticles within the Array of Thirteen Kills. They localize the golden Righteous Song that shields Zhou Dan in the source.

name: Vulture Peak
reason: The source peak name 'Vulture Peak' was carried over unchanged, as it already fits the Western fantasy register.
description: One of the Skyreach Sect's Thirty-Three Peaks and home of some competitors (master sheet). In Ep 260 its disciples are nearly struck by a stray golden beam during the competition; in the source it is the peak that launched a long-planned mountain challenge against Little Rain Peak.

name: Gold Flower Fan
reason: Pu Xingyu's 'golden fan', which spins out golden threads that weave into a giant net in the source, was localized as the 'Gold Flower Fan'.
description: Stanley's Spirit Weapon (Eps 261-262), a fan that draws out Vitality and projects razor-thin golden threads for his Golden Razornet technique. It corresponds to the golden fan wielded by Pu Xingyu in the aligned source chapters, whose interconnected golden threads form a huge entrapping net.

name: Master Oliver
reason: The character was given the US-style name 'Oliver' with the 'Master' honorific; his source counterpart (the master of Adrian's source equivalent in the aligned chapters) was not identified in the evidence.
description: Adrian the Arrogant's master, introduced around Ep 269 and described as protective and strategic. His expression darkens as he listens to reports, and Adrian bows deeply to him to announce a breakthrough.

name: Theo and Barnaby
reason: Conjoined mention of two separate characters (Theo, Barnaby), not an entity in itself; each name is covered individually.

name: Assassin’s Ten Commandments
reason: Localized name for the behavioral creed an assassin character recites to master his emotions; the source's exact term for this code was not identified in the evidence.
description: A creed of ten rules recited by an assassin character during the tournament arc (Eps 273-274); he clamps down on surging emotion by going back to reciting the Assassin's Ten Commandments.

name: Sky Arch
reason: An adaptation-coined landmark name giving the capital a Western monumental flavor; no source counterpart appears in the evidence.
description: A monumental arch at the entrance to the capital; Zane passes beneath it onto Capitol Drive while trying to absorb the city's magnificent sights (Ep 28).

name: Legacy Charter
reason: An adaptation term extending the show's 'Legacy House' terminology; no named source counterpart for this credential appears in the evidence.
description: A credential the fatigued administrator demands when Zane registers for the entrance exams in Ep 28; the term is unfamiliar to Zane. Apparently a document associated with the Legacy Houses.

name: Reaper’s Chop
reason: Likely localizes the layered-wave saber technique from the aligned source chapters (successive swings each release a wave of power, as in the 'Three Layered Waves' of the Tyrant Saber of the Heavens), renamed 'Reaper's Chop' for a punchier Western register.
description: Shayna's signature machete technique, honed through countless battles (Eps 280-281). Her successive roaring swings release immense, visible waves of power rippling from the weapon's edge, shaking the arena; the third swing carves the air with a thunderous whoosh.

name: Academy Trials
reason: Localized name for the trials that follow the entrance exam in the source's sect-admission process; the source's exact term was not identified in the evidence.
description: The trials that follow the main Entrance Exam (Ep 29); successfully navigating both the exam and the Academy Trials earns candidates the privilege of donning the Shadow Cloaks.

name: Seven-Star Herb
reason: The source's mythical 'Seven Star Grass' was localized as 'Seven-Star Herb' for the Western fantasy setting.
description: A mythical herb said to emit a seven-colored glow that nourishes and heals the soul when one gets close to it (Ep 291). Sir Kenneth doubts one could exist in the Eastern Territory, reasoning that a real Seven-Star Herb would change the color of the sky and land for miles and could never be hidden.

name: Marrow Refining Stage
issues: Ep 298 uses the raw source cultivation term 'Marrow Refining Stage' (in the sword-intent mountain scene), while the delivered episodes otherwise use the show's own localized tier names (Adept, Soul Realm, etc.) - likely an un-localized leak from the source.
reason: The source term 'Marrow Refining Stage' was carried over verbatim rather than mapped to the show's localized tier system.
description: A cultivation stage named in Ep 298: sword intent bursting from the sword mounds reveals that someone once reached the Consummation of sword intent while only at the Marrow Refining Stage - a genius considered a rarity anywhere in the world, hitting Zane like a physical blow.

name: Level Adept
reason: Extraction fragment of 'Nth-level Adept' tier phrasing, not a standalone entity.

name: Trent
reason: The source character Yu Qingcheng was fully localized as 'Trent Sutton'; the surname 'Sutton' also renames his family (the source's Yu Family) as House Sutton of the Seven Great Houses.
description: The subject of a cautionary tale told in Ep 302: a young prodigy of House Sutton, one of the Seven Great Houses of the Eastern Territories, whose deadly path made him ever more cruel and vicious until he had massacred countless people. His house looked the other way because of his rapid progress, until he killed two of its own men and they realized the Malice had consumed him, turning him into a mindless killing machine - matching the source's Yu Qingcheng, whom the Yu Family let kill as he pleased and of whom no news was heard after three years.

name: Killing Sword Mountain Zane
issues: Extraction artifact concatenating 'Killing Sword Mountain' with an adjacent mention of Zane; the underlying mentions belong to Killing Sword Mountain itself.

name: Roster
reason: The Skyreach Sect's disciple ranking list, apparently localizing the source sect's 'Honor Roll' rankings.
description: The Skyreach Sect's official disciple list and ranking. In Eps 317-318, Evan protests to Elder Gates against being kicked off the Roster before the All Peaks Competition after his breakthrough, insisting his name is still on the participants' list; he is noted as ranked high on the disciple Roster.

name: Preliminary Exam
reason: The source's preliminary selection round (rendered 'Sea Test' in the translation) was localized as the plainly descriptive 'Preliminary Exam'.
description: The qualifying round of the sect-admission process: passing it qualifies a candidate for the main Entrance Exam (Ep 32).

name: Chuck
reason: The antagonist lord was given the blunt US name 'Chuck', and his family became House Hawthorne; this recasts the source's Luo-clan elder Luo Junyi, father of the son Luo Zheng kills, as the lord of a rival house.
description: Lord of House Hawthorne and Darcy's father, reputedly the most powerful man in Castermere County at the fifth level of the Adept Realm; he somehow found the resources to let Darcy jump three power levels in a row (Eps 327-330). After Zane kills Darcy, Zane cuts off Chuck's right hand along with Ford's in Ep 336, leaving the two most respected fighters in the county on their knees, and Chuck is forced to compensate House Lowell. He corresponds to Luo Junyi in the aligned source chapters, whose eldest son Luo Chengyun died fighting Luo Zheng and who then turned the Thousand Forms Tribulation Thunder Halberd on Luo Zheng himself.

name: Kyle
reason: The source's palace elder 'Uncle Ya' was localized with the US-style name 'Kyle', keeping the 'Uncle' honorific used for trusted royal retainers.
description: Prince Ray's trusted follower and a royal-family elder (Eps 345-346). Short but muscular, he blocks Zane from leaving the Imperial Palace with the princess and fights him with a short spear - a low-class Sacred Weapon - batting aside Zane's superior swordsmanship with sheer Vitality-infused power. He matches the source's Uncle Ya, the palace elder who controls his fight with Luo Zheng through his dense True Essence.

name: Hendy
reason: A minor royal-faction follower given the US-style name 'Hendy'; his exact source counterpart was not identified in the evidence.
description: One of Ray's men (Eps 348-349), who like others in the prince's retinue has reached the primary level of the Inner-Core Realm.

name: Dakota Peaks
issues: Ep 35 calls the sect's training peaks the 'Dakota Peaks', while the master sheet elsewhere refers to the peak system as the Thirty-Three Peaks (e.g. Vulture Peak) - possible early-episode name drift for the same peak system.
reason: The source sect's system of rival training peaks (with its mountain-challenge rules) was collectively localized under the US-flavored name 'Dakota Peaks'.
description: Majestic, mist-shrouded mountains long designated by the Skyreach Sect as training grounds for its inner circle and pledges (Ep 35). An intricate, meticulously designed set of rules governs the rivalry between the peaks - a competition that extends beyond disciples to the instructors who stake their reputations on their students' achievements.

name: Crafting Skill
reason: Generic capitalized common-noun phrase, not a distinct named entity.

name: Grade Adept
reason: Extraction fragment of 'Nth-Grade Adept' tier phrasing (e.g. Fourth-Grade Adept), not a standalone entity.

name: Adepts and Soul Realm
reason: Conjoined fragment of two tier names (Adept, Soul Realm) already covered individually, not an entity in itself.

name: Hoffman
reason: A minor rival-sect disciple given the US-style name 'Hoffman'; his exact source counterpart among the rival sect disciples in the aligned chapters was not identified in the evidence.
description: The number-two disciple of the Crimson Sect, nearly on Alistair's level (Ep 357). His side considers sending him out against Zane, but Eddy restrains him from making the challenge.

name: Saint Morphen's Mystical Pace
reason: Localized name for the famed movement art Toby Dillon recognizes in Zane's footwork, following the source pattern of techniques named after legendary masters; the exact source technique was not identified in the evidence.
description: A legendary movement technique that Toby Dillon, drawing on decades of study, identifies as Zane navigates the Cloud Road (Ep 360). Per the master sheet it is related to Spatial Law perception.

name: Prismatic Gem Ring
reason: No source counterpart appears in the evidence; the name appears to be an adaptation coinage for the pill-dispensing ring in the scene.
description: A stunning ring set with five different colored jewels, worn by a female elder in Ep 37. Tapping a jewel dispenses a pill, such as the bright silver pill she pops out and casually tosses to the chief elder.

name: Darksteel
reason: Likely localizes a source metal used for the chest-guarding automatons and top-grade weapon forging in the treasure-chest arc; the exact source term was not identified in the evidence.
description: An extremely hard metal with a purplish sheen, among the hardest in existence and used to forge top-grade Sacred Weapons (Eps 376-379). The automatons guarding the treasure chests on the trial path are made of it, and a Darksteel automaton's blade nearly cost Zane his life at the silver chest.
